predecessors.name: Pajang Sultanate
predecessors.text: Pajang, whose last ruler submitted to Sutawijaya in 1586 (Mataram page: 'This event in 1586, marked the end of Pajang kingdom and the rise of its former vassal, the Mataram Sultanate')

successors.name: Surakarta Sunanate
successors.text: the Surakarta half of the Giyanti partition (Pakubuwono II's court at Surakarta from 1745/1746)

successors.name: Yogyakarta Sultanate
successors.text: the Yogyakarta half of the Giyanti partition, the Sultanate of Mangkubumi

successors.name: Dutch Republic
successors.text: the north coast (pasisir), East Java and Madura, which the VOC held by 1743: 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen'

ledger.x: 1584: Sutawijaya (Panembahan Senapati) makes Mataram independent of Pajang.
1586: Pajang ends and Mataram takes its lands.
1588: Cliopatria's first Mataram outline holds Madiun and Kediri.
1613: the court moves from Kota Gede to Karta as Sultan Agung takes the throne (infobox 'Karta (1613-1645)'; 'Sultan Agung became the ruler of Mataram in 1613').
1615: Agung takes Wirasaba, the first East Java conquest.
1616: Lasem falls.
1617: Pasuruan is taken.
1619: Tuban falls.
1622: Mataram captures Sukadana, which the page then lists among its vassals.
1624: Madura is taken after a fierce battle.
1625: Surabaya falls after five years of war.

c. 1625: Cirebon in Mataram's sphere. The page says only 'Agung himself took the hand of Cirebon Princess as his consort' (no year) and that Cirebon 'was forced to shift allegiance from Mataram to the Dutch' under Amangkurat II; 1625 is the page's year for Mataram ruling 'most of Java', a bridge.
1631: Mataram's hold on the Priangan is first shown by its suppression of rebellions: the page says Sumedang and Ukur were suppressed in 1631-1636.
1639: Blambangan surrenders.
1641: the ruler takes the Sultan's title.
1645: Sultan Agung dies (spring 1645) and, with him, the greatest extent.
1646: the court moves to Plered (infobox 'Plered (1646-1680)') under Amangkurat I; 'Agung died in the spring of 1645.'
1659: Blambangan regains its independence.

1676: Trunajaya's rebels take the north coast. the Trunajaya page has rebels take most northern coastal towns, from Surabaya to Cirebon, except Jepara (1676-1677), after the victory at Gegodog in September 1676.
1677: Kediri becomes the rebel base.
1677: Madura and the rest of the rebel coast return to Mataram and the VOC.
April 1677: Surabaya is retaken.
June 1677: the rebels take Plered.
September 1677: Amangkurat II, on VOC ships at Jepara, agrees to concessions.
25 November 1678: Kediri falls to VOC and Mataram forces under François Tack; the court of Amangkurat II is then set up at Surabaya. the page has Kediri fall on 25 November 1678.
1680: Plered is recovered. the Trunajaya page has, for September-November 1680, Amangkurat II building a new capital at Kartasura while the VOC and royal forces drove Puger out of Plered.
1680: the court moves to the new capital Kartasura (infobox 'Kartosuro (1680-1745)').

c. 1680: Cirebon leaves Mataram. The Mataram page, in Amangkurat II's reign, has 'Cirebon too was forced to shift allegiance from Mataram to the Dutch'; the Trunajaya page has Cirebon declaring independence with Banten's support in 1677-1678. The page gives no year for the shift.
August 1681: Puger retakes Plered. the Trunajaya page has, for August-November 1681, Puger retaking Plered and then being defeated in November and pardoned by his brother.
November 1681: Puger is defeated and pardoned by Amangkurat II, and Plered returns.
1705: the VOC receives Semarang.
1705: eastern Madura goes to the VOC.
1705: Mataram cedes its rights in Cirebon.
By 1743: the Chinese war leaves Mataram a Central Java interior.

1745: the court moves from Kartasura to Surakarta (infobox 'Surakarta (1745-1755)'; the text says Pakubuwana II 'built a new kraton in Surakarta or Solo and moved there in 1746', and Pakubuwono II's page gives no date).
1755: Mataram is partitioned at Giyanti.

wars.name: Mataram conquest of the Surabaya league
wars.outcome: Agung attacked Surabaya and Malang in 1614 and failed, then took Wirasaba (1615), Lasem (1616), Pasuruan (1617), Tuban (1619), Madura (1624) and, after five years of war, Surabaya (1625).

wars.name: Mataram expedition to Sukadana
wars.outcome: Mataram captured Sukadana, Surabaya's ally in southwest Kalimantan, in 1622 (Mataram page); the Tanjungpura page has Adipati Kendal's expedition attack Matan that year.

wars.name: Sieges of Batavia
wars.outcome: Agung's attempt to capture Batavia in 1628-1629 failed; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Suppression of Tembayat, Sumedang and Ukur
wars.outcome: Tembayat was crushed in 1630 and Sumedang and Ukur were suppressed in 1631-1636 (the page's wording).

wars.name: Mataram conquest of Blambangan
wars.outcome: Blambangan surrendered in 1639 and regained its independence in 1659.

wars.name: Trunajaya rebellion
wars.outcome: The VOC and Mataram crushed the rebels (Kediri 25 November 1678, Trunajaya's surrender 26 December 1679); Amangkurat II received the VOC's price in the September 1677 concessions and moved to Kartasura in 1680; Puger was pardoned in November 1681.

wars.name: First Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: it 'dragged on for five years before the Dutch managed to install Pakubuwana' I (Mataram page); in 1705 Mataram agreed to cede Cirebon and eastern Madura and the VOC was given Semarang.

wars.name: Second Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: The page gives only the dates (the Mataram page: 1719-1723) and no territorial result.

wars.name: Chinese War (Java War of 1740-1743)
wars.outcome: The rebels took Kartasura on 30 June 1742; the northern coast was cleared of rebels by October 1742 with the VOC; 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen'.

wars.name: Third Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: Mangkubumi rose in May 1746 (the page dates the war 1749-1755); it ended with the Giyanti agreement of 1755, which divided Mataram between the Surakarta Sunanate and the Yogyakarta Sultanate.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary: Java's interior and coast are drawn from Cliopatria's outlines and circles round named towns.
